content_voiceover: This slide comes from the Taiwan Hemophilia Treatment Guidelines and introduces the concept of comprehensive care. The key message up top is that hemophilia is a rare, complex inherited disorder, and optimal management, especially for people with severe disease, requires much more than just treating acute bleeding episodes when they happen. It needs a coordinated, ongoing care model. Below that, you see two prevalence tables side by side, one for the globe and one specific to Taiwan. Globally, the prevalence is about twenty-one cases per one hundred thousand males for all hemophilia combined, and about thirty cases per one hundred thousand male births when you look at prevalence at birth. In Taiwan, those numbers are noticeably lower, roughly ten per one hundred thousand overall and fifteen per one hundred thousand at birth, close to half the global rate. This kind of regional variation is worth noting, since local registries can differ from global pooled estimates, and it has implications for national resource planning and comprehensive care programs.
keypoints: Comprehensive hemophilia care means more than treating acute bleeds, especially in severe disease
Global prevalence is about 21 per 100,000 males for all hemophilia
Taiwan's reported prevalence, about 10 per 100,000, is roughly half the global rate
Regional registries can differ meaningfully from global pooled estimates
keypoint_voiceover: The big picture here is that comprehensive care goes beyond acute bleed management, and that Taiwan's local prevalence numbers run lower than the global estimates, about half in both the overall and at-birth figures. Know that regional registries can differ meaningfully from global pooled data.
